text: Brisk means quick and full of energy. When people say business is brisk, they mean sales are coming in fast and customers keep arriving. Here the little toy shop is busy enough that postmen come through the door three times a day.

Fertile soil is soil where plants grow easily and well. People borrow the word for any place or situation where something spreads fast, like fertile ground for an idea. Calling Britain fertile ground means this new way of selling caught on there quickly.

Someone who is ailing is sick and not getting better. Writers also use it for businesses and towns that are weak and struggling. Britain's ailing high street means its town shopping streets have been losing shops for years.

An entrepreneur is someone who starts their own business instead of taking a job at someone else's. They put in their own money and time, and they keep the profits if it works or lose out if it does not. The word comes from French and is said on-truh-pruh-NUR.

In Britain the high street is the main shopping street in the middle of a town, with the bakery, the bank and the shoe shop on it. Americans call the same thing Main Street. When news stories say the high street, they usually mean all of a country's town-centre shops at once, not one particular street.

TikTok Shop is a part of the TikTok app that lets you buy something you see in a video without ever leaving the app. The seller lists the product, you tap and pay, and TikTok takes a cut of the sale. It started in Asia and has spread fast in Britain.

Live commerce means selling things during a live video stream. A seller goes on camera, shows the products, answers questions in the comments, and viewers buy while they watch. It began in China, where it is a normal way to shop, and Britain has picked it up faster than most countries.

A stream here is not a small river. In this sense a stream is a video being sent out live over the internet as it happens. A shopping stream is one where the point of the video is selling you something.

Gen Z is short for Generation Z, meaning people born roughly between 1997 and 2012. It is a band of birth years, not an age, so a person keeps the label for life. Most middle-schoolers today are actually one step past it, in Generation Alpha.

Millennials are people born roughly between 1981 and 1996, the group just before Gen Z. They are named for growing up around the year 2000, the millennium. In 2026 that makes them about 30 to 45 years old, so most of them are parents rather than teenagers.

QVC is a television channel that does nothing but sell things. Presenters hold up jewellery, gadgets or clothes, talk about them for several minutes, and viewers phone in to order. It has been running since the 1980s, which is why the article compares it to shopping on TikTok.

Something mesmeric is so oddly gripping that you keep watching even though nothing much is happening. It comes from Franz Mesmer, an eighteenth-century doctor who claimed he could put people into trances. Calling QVC mesmeric means viewers get stuck watching it for hours.

Obsessiveness is the habit of thinking about one thing far more than most people would. An obsession is the thing itself, and obsessiveness is the quality of being that way. Here it describes fans who cannot stop watching the shopping videos.

To traipse is to walk in and out in a tired, unhurried, back-and-forth way. It usually suggests more trips than anyone wanted to make. Postmen traipsing through the door means they keep coming and going all day.
Postmen is the British word for the people who deliver and collect the mail. Americans say mail carriers or mailmen. In Britain the post means the mail, and the Post Office runs it.

To dispatch someone is to send them off to do a particular job. It can also mean sending out a package or a message. Here a customer has been dispatched by his daughter, meaning she sent him to the shop on an errand.

To reckon is to work something out roughly, or simply to think so. It is very common in British English where an American would say figures or guesses. The butcher reckons 60% of his TikTok customers are older women, meaning that is his estimate.

A queue is a line of people waiting their turn, and it is the normal British word for it. It is said like the letter Q. Four-hour queues outside the shop means people stand in line for four hours to get in.
Commerce means buying and selling, taken as a whole activity rather than one purchase. E-commerce is buying and selling online. This sort of commerce means this whole way of shopping.

To embrace someone is to hug them. Used about ideas, it means to take something up gladly instead of resisting it. British consumers embraced live commerce means they were happy to try this way of shopping.

Viral first meant caused by a virus, as in a viral infection. Online it means something that spreads from person to person very fast, the way an illness does. Viral brands are products that became popular because videos of them were shared everywhere.
Declined here does not mean said no. This is the other meaning: got smaller, weaker or worse over time. Britain's high streets have declined means they have steadily lost shops and shoppers.

To revive something is to bring it back to life or back to strength after it has faded. Doctors revive a patient whose heart has stopped; a town can be revived by new businesses. The question at the top of the article is whether TikTok sellers could revive the high street.

Stock here does not mean shares in a company or soup base. In a shop, stock is all the goods sitting there waiting to be sold. Shelves packed with brightly coloured stock means the shop is full of toys ready to go out.

A stock take is when a shop counts everything it actually has on its shelves and in its storeroom. The count is compared with what the records say should be there, which catches thefts, breakages and mistakes. Most shops do one at least once a year, often after hours.
Firm here is a noun, not the adjective meaning hard or solid. A firm is a business or company. The firm ships worldwide and has 14 staff means the toy shop as a business does those things.

A line in business means a group of related products sold under one name, like a clothing line. Funky's own lower-cost line is a set of cheaper toys the shop designs and sells itself. It has nothing to do with a line you stand in.

Accountancy is the British word for accounting, the job of keeping track of a business's money. Accountants record what comes in and goes out, work out the tax owed, and check the books add up. Alex is studying it at school while running her shop.

In England, sixth form is the last two years of school, for students aged about 16 to 18, after the exams taken at 16. A sixth-form college is a school that teaches only those two years. It is roughly the equivalent of American 11th and 12th grade.

Pick and pack is the warehouse job of collecting the right items off the shelves for an order and boxing them up to post. Big companies hide this work in windowless warehouses. The surprise here is that TikTok sellers film themselves doing it and people enjoy watching.

In real time means as it actually happens, with no delay and no editing. A recorded video can be cut and sped up; a real-time one shows you the minutes as they pass. Watching staff pack your order in real time means you see it happening live.

To turn up somewhere is to arrive, especially when it was not certain you would. It can also mean something lost is found again. Followers willing to turn up to physical shops means they actually travel there in person.

Far afield means a long way away from home. As far afield as is the usual way to introduce the most distant example in a list. Customers from as far afield as London and Edinburgh means some travelled hundreds of miles.

To give something a lift is to raise it up, cheer it up or improve it. In Britain a lift is also an elevator, and a lift in a car is a ride, so the word works hard. Giving the high street a lift means helping struggling shops do better.

Funky Fidgets is the real shop this article is about, in Darlington in northern England. It sells sensory toys, meaning fidget spinners, stress balls and squishy things people hold to keep their hands busy. Alex started it at 11 during the pandemic and it now has 14 staff.

The Fat Butcher is a butcher's shop about 70km north of Darlington that also sells on TikTok. A butcher is a shop or person that cuts and sells meat. It is used here as a second example, to show this is not only happening with toys.

Darlington is a town in the north-east of England, with around 100,000 people. It is famous in history as one end of the world's first proper passenger railway, opened in 1825. It is not a place tourists normally visit, which is why the shop owner's remark about bringing tourism in is a joke worth noticing.
